  "research_problem": "Existing models in this five-paper corpus do not consistently predict mechanical response across both compliant and stiffened states.   "research_question": "For one hybrid SMP–layer-jamming continuum finger, does a geometrically nonlinear finite-element model incorporating hyperelastic elastomer behavior, explicit passive envelope/heater layers, and frictional interlayer contact reduce held-out normalized RMSE in tip force and tangent bending stiffness by at least 30% relative to a simplified E(T)I(P) baseline across 25–75 °C, 0 to −100 kPa vacuum, and both jammed and unjammed loading states?",
  "proposed_contribution": "A validated mechanics model and parameter-identification protocol for one hybrid variable-stiffness continuum-finger platform, together with quantified accuracy gains and clearly reported failure regimes across temperature, vacuum pressure, deformation, and stiffness state.   "falsification_checks": [
    "Reject the proposed accuracy advantage if the nonlinear model fails to reduce held-out tip-force and tangent-stiffness NRMSE by at least 30% relative to the baseline.",
    "Test whether improvement persists on load cases excluded from calibration; failure on held-out conditions indicates overfitting rather than better mechanics.",
    "Perform ablation models that separately remove the passive layers, hyperelasticity, and frictional contact. If removal does not materially degrade held-out prediction, the corresponding proposed mechanism is not supported.",
    "Repeat validation separately in jammed and unjammed states. A pooled improvement that masks failure in either state does not support the unified-model claim.",
